title: Introduction to the complete new features of the CLO7.3 patch version (latest update January 30, 2024)

summary: ```markdown # Introduction to the Complete New Features of the CLO 7.3 Patch Version **Latest Update: January 30, 2024** --- ## Overview Hello everyone, today I would like to introduce you to CLO 7.3, a new feature designed in the updated version released 30 days later. There are seven modules in total, which are the main functions, 2D, 3D, virtual model, color, rendering, and mode. ## Main Function: Everywhere First of all, let's talk about the main function, **Everywhere**. From the beginning, the Everywhere function can be easily optimized in CLO for various digital spaces, such as games, the round universe, and entertainment spaces. The Everywhere function is currently in the testing stage, and all users who pre-register on the Connect webpage can use it. Pre-registration can be done on the Connect webpage under the Everywhere option and is currently unlimited and open. **Please note:** Everywhere is a test function, and the policy of use may change in the future. ### Using Everywhere In this example, we will guide you to use Everywhere to complete the process of testing clothes, network optimization, binding skeleton, UV fill, and baking patterns. In the software interface, click on the icon in the upper right corner to open Everywhere. The Everywhere window appears in the upper right corner of the 2D version of the test window. The number of multidirectional network spaces for clothes and virtual models is displayed in the lower left corner of the 3D window. The Everywhere window is divided into two options: clothes and materials. - **Clothes Option:** You can optimize the multidirectional network space and bind the skeleton. - **Material Option:** You can perform operations such as UV filling, baking patterns, and material application. ## Multidirectional Network Optimization ### Clothing Option First, let's take a look at the multidirectional network optimization in the clothing option. Multidirectional refers to the network that constitutes the clothing. When you share your creations on different platforms, the number and capacity of the support network may differ. Therefore, considering the different functions of each platform, you can use the multidirectional network optimization function to maintain the 3D clothing form. Before the optimization process is carried out, you can check the total network space of the current clothing. In the Everywhere window, the number on the right side of the clothing indicates the current network space of the clothing. This number includes the number of buttons or accessories on the clothing. Additionally, in the next virtual model column, you can check the multidirectional network space of the virtual model. ### How to Optimize the Multidirectional Network To optimize the multidirectional network: 1. In the clothing option in the multidirectional network optimization, enter the required multidirectional network number in the blank box on the left. 2. Click optimize to apply the customized multidirectional network to the specified number. If the accessory or button is a high-quality model, it can be done individually. Select the button or accessory to be used in the material window. After selecting, enter the required value into the technology box in the multidirectional network optimization at the bottom of the attribute editor window. This will optimize the multidirectional network of the accessory to match the specified number. ## Binding Skeleton Next, I will explain the option of binding the skeleton. The binding skeleton is in the 3D virtual model. It is a process of creating a similar skeleton structure so that it can be linked and moved. In the binding skeleton function of Everywhere, the binding skeleton can promote the synchronization of the created clothing and virtual model. This design connects the skeleton joints of the created virtual model with the clothing, ensuring that the movement of the clothing and virtual model is synchronized. The binding skeleton of Everywhere is specifically suitable for the human virtual model with joints. When the virtual model is in A or T-shape, it can run effectively. Under these conditions, the Binding Google function will automatically bind the clothing according to the binding information in the virtual model. Click the App button in the Binding Google column to apply the Binding Google function. ### Confirming Binding Google Function To confirm whether the Binding Google function is applied, we can apply a few poses. Once the Binding Google function is completed, the crowd will be applied to the clothing, allowing it to be switched with the virtual model during the pose change. When applying a different pose, you can observe the seamless switching between the clothing and the virtual model. **Warning Message:** When the Binding Google function is applied, a warning message will appear. If you choose "Yes," the clothing will be simulated, and the Binding Google information will be deleted. On the contrary, if you choose "No," the clothing will be simulated, and the Binding Google information will be retained. ## Brush Tool for Joint Movement After applying the Binding Google function, a new option will appear in this column. When you click on the update button, the clothing will be bound to Google again according to its current state. To modify joint movements, click on the brush tool. The Everywhere window will close for a short time, and a blood-like window related to the brush tool will appear in the same position. The purpose of the brush tool is to make it easy to modify. When activating the tool, the 3D clothing will automatically switch to the white texture, and the joints become visible. ### Adjusting the Brush Tool The tool can be adjusted in detail, allowing you to set the extent to which each part of the clothing is affected by the virtual model joint movement. Use the brush tool to adjust each part of the clothing to reflect the joint movement of the virtual model. Press the control key on the keyboard to make joint selection, which conveniently allows you to automatically confirm the weight of each joint. The brush window is composed of two options: weight and carving. Let's first take a look at the weight option. ## Weight Option In the weight option, you can use the brush tool to adjust the extent to which the online grid of clothing is bound to Google. Here, the weight refers to the influence or increase of the online grid. The brush tool can also modify the process of weight selection of certain areas on the clothing, which is called weight selection. After weight selection, a smoother and more natural movement can be be shown, allowing various poses to be switched seamlessly. ### Importance of Weight Selection Although automatic binding of the bone grid will automatically divide the weight, it is essential to perform weight selection operations when adjusting joints or poses to ensure that clothing moves naturally along the body. The brush tool can allow you to check or modify areas of clothing that may not be correct when modifying clothing or after changing joints or postures, ensuring the clothing follows the movement of the body. ### Combination Mode of the Weight Brush The combination mode of the weight brush provides three options: increase, decrease, and smooth. You can use the shortcut keys to control and tab to switch. Increase will increase the weight, decrease will decrease the weight, and smooth will adjust the weight value to balance the surrounding area. In the properties of the brush, you can adjust the strength, size, hardness, and depth. The strength can be set to the strength of the brush. You can use the slider or shortcut keys to adjust the size. The size can be set to the size of the brush, with shortcut keys being the left and right middle brackets. The hardness can be adjusted to the strength difference between the center of the brush and the edge. Finally, the depth represents the depth of the brush. You can reset the properties of the brush by pressing the reset button. ## Adjusting the Weight with the Brush Tool Now, let's use the weight brush described above to adjust the weight. In the 3D window, press the Ctrl key and press the joints of the virtual model to check the corresponding weight assigned to these joints. The color display follows red, green, and blue. In this row, the red area represents the higher weight distribution, while the blue area represents the lower weight distribution. The weight value is zero in the area where the color is not displayed. The more weight assigned to a specific area, the greater the influence in the animation process, helping to control the movement more smoothly and naturally. ### Using the Brush in the 2D Window In addition, you can also use the brush in the 2D version of the window to adjust the weight. When you open the window, you can see the virtual model joints. You can select the joints, move them, or use pre-made posture to confirm whether the clothes can penetrate or follow the unnatural body area. When you find that an area needs to be modified, you can adjust the fusion mode and brush properties, increasing or decreasing the weight of the brush to match the weight of the brush. If you find that a specific point, the peak point, and the weight around the weight are clearly different, you can use the weight hammer. This function will automatically adjust the weight of the point, making it more similar to its adjacent position. ### Using the Weight Hammer To use the weight hammer, press the Shift key and the desired peak point. When you press the Shift key, the mouse light will change from brush shape to a red dot, allowing you to identify the peak point.
